name: stroke overview
title: A sudden focal deficit runs the stroke protocol: glucose, NIH Stroke Scale and localization, then a non-contrast CT; no blood means an ischemic stroke (CT angiogram and perfusion, tPA within 4.5 hours, thrombectomy for a proximal large-vessel occlusion with a mismatch) or a TIA (CT, ASA, TIA clinic), both followed by secondary prevention chosen by cause; blood means an intracerebral hemorrhage (cause by site, BP under 160/110, hold antithrombotics) or a subarachnoid hemorrhage (vessel imaging, neurosurgery)

root.title: Sudden focal neurological deficit: STROKE PROTOCOL · TIME IS BRAIN
lines: point-of-care glucose (low sugar mimics a stroke) · 2 IV lines, labs (INR, creatinine, CBC) · NIH Stroke Scale
LOCALIZE before you look at the scan · door to imaging under 25 min, door to needle under 60 min
NON-CONTRAST CT first: any hemorrhage is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to tPA

groups.title: BLOOD: HEMORRHAGIC
lines: may not follow a territory · more often with a headache

head: h
Ischemic stroke
large vessel occlusion, or small vessel (lacunar)
clue: • LEFT MCA: aphasia + right face, arm > leg
• RIGHT MCA: left neglect, anosognosia + left face, arm > leg
• ACA: opposite leg · PCA: opposite hemianopsia
inv: dead brain · over 1/3 of MCA → no tPA
tx: First check: NO tPA if ANY
• hemorrhage now or ever · SAH symptoms, seizure at onset
• INR over 1.4 · PTT over 40 s · platelets under 100,000
• factor Xa inhibitor in 24-48 h · glucose under 3 or over 22
proximal occlusion + mismatch, even without tPA

head: h
Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
usually under 1 hour · NO infarct
clue: • e.g. 10 minutes of face and hand weakness
inv: echo · Holter · CTA or carotid Dopplers · lipids, glucose, BP
tx: already on ASA → add clopidogrel for 21 days

head: h
Intracerebral hemorrhage
bleeding into the brain
inv: also tumour (metastasis) · AVM, cavernoma, aneurysm · coagulopathy
after: repeat CT · no clot extension → heparin prophylaxis · rehabilitation

head: h
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
ruptured aneurysm, in most (or trauma)
clue: • sudden, explosive, worst headache of her life
inv: CTA or MRA to find the aneurysm
tx: coil or clip, by the aneurysm's shape and site

rows: SECONDARY PREVENTION, chosen by the CAUSE
admit to the stroke unit: BP watch and imaging at 24 h, nothing by mouth until a swallowing assessment · rehabilitation beats even tPA
• CARDIOEMBOLIC (atrial fibrillation, valve) → ANTICOAGULATE, ~2 weeks after
• all other causes → ASA 81 mg · clopidogrel if ASA fails
• symptomatic carotid stenosis over 70% → endarterectomy or stent
• BP under 140/90 · high-dose statin · glucose · smoking
